title: The Anglish Language: A Language for Programming for AI with AI
content: As AI coders grow more capable, English is becoming a common way to write software. Prompting an AI coder saves time, but it leaves the programmer with little understanding of the code it produced, and the gap widens each time the software changes. Anglish (Agent English) is a programming language for building software with AI coders that addresses this problem directly. Its central idea is to divide a problem into small parts and to state in English what each part is meant to do. AI coders then write the code for each part, while the programmer keeps a clear picture of the whole program as it evolves. Spaces, agents and paths are the main ways of imposing this structure on the author's intents. Spaces divide the program into parts, paths connect them, and agents and tasks inside each space do the work. The structure lets the programmer use the full power of AI coders without giving up oversight, even when complex software is built in a short time. Anglish has a gentle learning curve, yet it is expressive enough for programs from simple applications to large distributed systems, in many domains. The Anglish compiler produces an executable that runs on the Anglish virtual machine (angVM). The machine enforces the checks the author wrote every time the program runs, including after the program is changed to meet new requirements. The machine has data types and standard tasks for common interactions, but the author never names them. The author writes in English, and a decision model resolves each intent to one of the machine's choices, reporting an error when it cannot. This report describes the Anglish language, and a companion report describes the compiler and the virtual machine.
